name: Claude-BugHunter
cost: Free and open source (MIT for code, CC BY 4.0 for content)
works_with: Claude Code, OpenCode, Codex CLI, Hermes Agent and Google AntiGravity
short: A bundle of 83 skills and 15 slash commands for authorized bug bounty and external red-team work.
what: Claude-BugHunter is a skill bundle for bug hunting and external red-team engagements. It holds 83 skills drawn from 681 disclosed reports, covering web bug classes, recon, enterprise platform attack chains, and report writing. The skills load by topic when you describe what you are testing, and a 7-question gate checks scope before anything is submitted.
who: Security researchers on bug bounty programs and pentesters with a signed engagement. It covers the internet-facing attack surface only, so internal Active Directory, C2 and post-exploitation work are out of scope. If you do not have permission to test a target, this is not for you.
needs: Claude Code for the plugin route, or another supported agent for the copy install
Written permission to test the target: an in-scope bug bounty asset, a pentest engagement letter, a CTF or your own systems
Optional: Burp Suite with its MCP server extension

steps.title: Install the plugin
steps.text: All skills and commands load under the `claude-bughunter:` name.

steps.title: Or copy the skills in from a clone
steps.text: Clone the repo, go into its folder, then run the install script. On Windows use `pwsh ./scripts/install.ps1`. This route also gives you the `hunt` engagement scaffolder.

steps.title: Run the installer
steps.text: On macOS or Linux, from inside the cloned folder.

steps.title: Install for other agents too
steps.text: `--all` copies the skills to every agent it finds, and `--burp-mcp` wires in the Burp MCP server.

try.label: From the README
try.text: Testing acme.com, an in-scope HackerOne target. Run recon and rank the surface.

watch: The README limits it to assets you own or have written permission to test.
The skills run real recon and attack tools against the target you name, so check the scope of your program before each session.
The README says AI providers may refuse or switch models on offensive security requests, even authorized ones. It points to the provider's verification program for this.
The copy install writes into `~/.claude/` and the skill folders of any other agents it detects.
